title: Bound silent Polymarket WebSocket reconnects and serialize initial subscriptions
author: agent:/root

scope.goal: Implement the immediately preceding client-side WebSocket recovery correction: a reconnecting Polymarket shard must not be reported recovered while its socket is open but has delivered no frame, it must leave that silent state after a bounded first-frame wait instead of relying on the 90-second watchdog, and dynamic subscription updates must not race ahead of the initial subscription sequence.
inScope: Prospective local C#/.NET changes to the shared Polymarket market WebSocket shard runner, configuration, validation, focused tests and documentation; the user retains deployment control.

A configurable MarketDataWebSocket.FirstFrameTimeoutSeconds with exact default and service value 10 seconds, measured after every initial-subscription batch has been sent for the connection generation.

Readiness on the first complete non-empty inbound text frame, observed immediately after full transport receipt and before Maker admission, parsing or application dispatch, consistently with the existing transport last-message timestamp semantics.

Connecting status until readiness; first-frame timeout aborts that socket, emits and persists an explicit bounded FirstFrameTimeout/FirstFrameWait diagnostic, and returns to the existing reconnect loop and backoff.

A connection-generation subscription barrier that prevents dynamic subscribe/unsubscribe writes before the initial sequence completes and preserves desired asset changes that arrive during initialization.
Focused deterministic tests, Release service build, requirement validation, documentation and independent semantic review in a marked D:/CodexTemp run.
outOfScope: Any Production or application Local database access/mutation, service start/stop/restart, strategy/order/configuration mutation, deployment, backup or live-order action.

Eliminating, interpreting or claiming the remote cause of Polymarket close status 1013; changing endpoint, selected assets, subscription scope, shard allocation/count, subscription batch size or remote-provider policy.

Changing heartbeat cadence, reconnect delays, reconnect-backoff reset rules, StaleAfterSeconds, the post-readiness 90-second watchdog, or adding a ConnectAsync timeout or post-first-frame idle/read timeout.

Changing frame parsing, FIFO/no-drop handoff, Maker admission, side-effect queues, strategy decisions, execution intent, Paper/Live behavior, fills, settlement, accounting, PnL, balances or risk rules.

Treating binary, close or empty messages as readiness; requiring parse or application-dispatch success for transport readiness; guaranteeing a total recovery time because connect latency, existing backoff, repeated remote failures and provider availability remain outside this fix.
Schema/migration/package changes, a generalized WebSocket framework, unrelated refactoring or cleanup.
scope.periodOrFilter: Prospective behavior only after a future user-controlled deployment. The evidence window is the production process that started 2026-09-16T08:19:45.795511Z; no historical records are changed.
scope.firstVerification: Inspect the current runner's connection/status/heartbeat/close path, subscription update ordering, configuration validation and focused tests; confirm the observed 95-second episode was not a close-drain delay and preserve unrelated dirty files.

requirements.text: Require first-frame readiness and reconnect an open-but-silent Polymarket shard after exactly 10 seconds instead of waiting for the 90-second watchdog.
acceptanceCriteria: Add MarketDataWebSocket.FirstFrameTimeoutSeconds with a code default and explicit appsettings value of 10. Validation requires a positive value and, when WatchdogStaleSeconds is enabled, a value strictly below WatchdogStaleSeconds; the startup configuration summary and documentation expose the value.

After ConnectAsync and all initial-subscription batches succeed, the connection remains Connecting. Socket State=Open, subscription-send completion and outbound heartbeat activity must not publish Connected or count as readiness.

The first complete non-empty inbound text frame marks transport readiness immediately after full receipt, before channel waiting, Maker admission, parsing and application dispatch. This uses the existing transport-liveness meaning of lastMessageUtc; malformed or zero-update text may still prove transport receipt while retaining their existing parse/dispatch diagnostics and without resetting reconnect backoff unless the existing accepted-update rule does so.

The 10-second timer begins only after the full initial-subscription sequence completes. If readiness is not observed before it expires, the exact socket is aborted, a warning and persisted API diagnostic identify Reason=FirstFrameTimeout and Phase=FirstFrameWait with component, attempt, subscribed count, timeout and socket state but no raw frame or secret, and the existing reconnect loop/backoff continues.

A close or connection failure before readiness follows the existing immediate close/failure path; service cancellation propagates without a timeout warning. After readiness, existing receive/dispatch, heartbeat, stale/watchdog and reconnect-reset semantics remain unchanged.

Deterministic tests prove no early Connected state, readiness on transport receipt before a blocked consumer, timeout abort/diagnostic/reconnect propagation, close-before-readiness, cancellation, and unchanged accepted-update reconnect-backoff reset behavior.

verification.expected: All focused readiness, timeout, cancellation, diagnostic, reconnect-backoff and configuration tests pass without an external WebSocket or application database.
verification.evidence: The final approved Release filter passed 98/98 tests with 0 failures and 0 skipped. It covers first non-empty transport-frame readiness before blocked dispatch, empty-frame exclusion, exact 10-second timeout, atomic frame-versus-timeout winner claims in both orders, one abort, close and cancellation behavior, explicit diagnostic wiring, unchanged accepted-update reconnect-backoff behavior, and configuration defaults/validation/summary. Because an existing disconnect source-contract locator assumes repository-relative artifacts, its current runner source was mirrored only inside the marked run's test layout; no repository file or runtime behavior was changed by that bounded test-layout workaround.

requirements.text: Serialize dynamic asset-subscription changes behind the complete initial subscription for each connection generation without losing changes made during initialization.
acceptanceCriteria: No UpdateAssetsAsync subscribe/unsubscribe write may be sent on a connection generation before every initial-subscription batch for that generation has completed.

Asset additions/removals arriving during connect or initial send are retained as the latest desired set and reconciled against the exact set sent initially before that generation is declared ready; alternatively that generation is explicitly aborted so the next initial subscription uses the latest desired set. No change is silently lost.
All outbound subscription writes remain serialized. A failed, closed, cancelled or superseded connection generation cannot receive a later dynamic update.
The existing subscription scope, asset selector, batching, shard plan and post-barrier dynamic update meaning remain unchanged.

Deterministic tests cover an update held behind initial subscription, additions and removals arriving during initialization, failure/cancellation, no write to an old generation, and preservation of send ordering.

verification.expected: All subscription-generation barrier, delta reconciliation, ordering, cancellation and old-generation exclusion tests pass deterministically.
verification.evidence: The final 98/98 approved filter includes deterministic MarketDataWebSocketFrameProcessingTests for complete initial-batch ordering, updates held behind initialization, latest desired-set addition/removal reconciliation, initialization failure and cancellation, and rejection of sends through a deactivated old generation.

acceptanceCriteria: README and configuration reference document the 10-second first-frame readiness rule, subscription barrier, unchanged post-readiness watchdog/backoff, and the limitation that remote 1013 closes may continue.

The focused tests and Release service build pass using a marked D:/CodexTemp run with TEMP/TMP/TMPDIR and explicit artifacts/results paths; no service is started and no application database or external exchange fixture is used.
